evals.prompt: Help me create a LinkedIn content strategy. I'm a SaaS founder building in public and want to grow my personal brand to drive awareness for my product. I currently have 500 followers and post maybe once a week.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should establish content pillars (3-5) appropriate for a SaaS founder building in public: industry insights, behind-the-scenes, educational content, personal stories, promotional (minimal). Should apply the platform quick reference for LinkedIn (3-5x/week recommended, carousels and stories perform well). Should provide hook formulas for LinkedIn posts. Should create a weekly content calendar. Should include engagement strategy (daily 30-min routine). Should address going from 1x/week to 3-5x/week with a batching strategy.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Establishes 3-5 content pillars
Applies LinkedIn platform guidance
Provides hook formulas
Creates weekly content calendar
Includes engagement strategy
Addresses batching strategy for consistency
Recommends increasing from 1x to 3-5x per week

evals.prompt: Write me a Twitter/X thread about the lessons I learned bootstrapping my SaaS to $10k MRR. Include hooks and a CTA at the end.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the hook formulas for a story hook (e.g., '6 months ago, I had $0 MRR. Today, I hit $10k.'). Should structure the thread following platform best practices: strong hook in tweet 1, each tweet should stand alone but flow together, use specific numbers and stories, end with a CTA. Should reference the content pillar this fits into (behind-the-scenes / founder journey). Should provide the actual thread content with 8-12 tweets. Should include engagement prompts.
assertions: Applies hook formulas from the skill
Uses a story hook for the first tweet
Structures thread with standalone but flowing tweets
Uses specific numbers and stories
Ends with clear CTA
Provides 8-12 tweet thread content
Includes engagement prompts

Applies content repurposing system

Provides format for LinkedIn, Twitter/X, and Instagram

Diagnoses potential engagement issues
Addresses hook quality
Addresses posting timing
Recommends daily engagement routine
Suggests trying different content formats
Provides specific before/after hook examples

evals.prompt: I want to turn our new pricing guide into a LinkedIn carousel. It has 9 negotiation tactics for SaaS buyers. Help me structure the slides.
evals.expected_output: Should load references/carousel-frameworks.md and pick a framework BEFORE writing slides — a list of 9 named tactics maps to Hack List (or Value-Stack; should justify the choice), not Rant Callout or Demo Walkthrough. Should produce a slide-by-slide structure: contrarian or exact-count cover (slide 1 written as a standalone scroll-stopper), one named tactic per slide, and a synthesis + single-CTA close. Should apply LinkedIn document-post notes (PDF upload, denser text tolerated, post text written as its own hook rather than 'see attached'). Should keep any count promised on the cover exactly delivered and flag that stats/claims must be real. Should mention judging performance on saves/completion rather than likes.
assertions: Loads or applies the carousel-frameworks reference
Selects an appropriate framework (Hack List or Value-Stack) with a stated reason before drafting slides
Slide 1 is written as a standalone scroll-stopper with the count or contrarian claim
One tactic/idea per slide, each named
Final slide has a synthesis and exactly one CTA
Applies LinkedIn document-post guidance (PDF, post text as its own hook)
Does not invent stats or pad the tactic count

evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing that our invoicing tool now syncs with QuickBooks. Make it punchy so it gets engagement.
evals.expected_output: Should write a post that leads with a specific hook (a fact, number, or customer situation) and avoids AI tells even though 'punchy' and 'engagement' invite them. No contrast reveals, no 'no X, no Y, no Z' lists, no self-answered questions or colon reveals, no em dashes. No broetry (one sentence per line for the whole post), no engagement-bait closer ('Agree?', 'Thoughts?', 'Let that sink in'), no emoji bullets. Ends on the point or a real question.
assertions: No contrast reveal or negation list
No em dashes
Not written as broetry
No engagement-bait closer
Hook is specific rather than a generic pattern-interrupt

evals.prompt: I'm posting on X 5 times every morning between 9 and 10am and my reach keeps dropping. I mostly post quick thoughts and hot takes. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the X algorithm reference (references/x-algorithm.md). Should identify post clustering as the primary problem: the author-diversity scorer decays scores of repeated authors within a feed response, so 5 posts in an hour cannibalize each other — recommend spacing original posts ~60 minutes apart or spreading across the day. Should also check hook mechanics (specific claim in the first 8 words, topic named early so topic-based distribution can route the post) and presence (staying available to reply for the first 30 minutes after each post rather than batch-firing and leaving). Should reframe goals toward DM-shares, follows, and profile clicks rather than likes, since those are separately scored signals. Should note weight values are unpublished and recommendations are directional.
assertions: References X algorithm mechanics from x-algorithm.md
Identifies post clustering / author-diversity decay as the main issue
Recommends ~60 minute spacing between original posts
Addresses hook structure (specific claim in first 8 words)
Mentions topic-anchoring for topic-based distribution
Recommends being present to reply after posting
Reframes toward shares/follows/profile clicks over likes

evals.prompt: Write an X post announcing our new AI feature. Draft: 'We're so excited to announce something HUGE is coming... 🔥🔥 You won't want to miss this. Like and retweet if you're ready!!'
evals.expected_output: Should rewrite rather than lightly edit, and explain why using X ranking mechanics: the draft has no specific claim in the first 8 words, doesn't name the topic (so topic-based distribution can't route it), names nothing specific (no product, no capability), and 'like and retweet if you're ready' is engagement bait — the algorithm predicts negative actions (not interested, mute, block) and subtracts them, and baity phrasing risks muted-keyword filtering. Rewrite should open with the specific capability and name the product/tools involved, make the post DM-forwardable (specific, useful claim), and optionally suggest posting mechanics: don't cluster with other posts, stay present for the first 30 minutes, and if including video make it 8+ seconds with captions.
assertions: Rewrites the post rather than approving it
Flags the missing specific claim in the first 8 words
Flags engagement bait and explains predicted negative-action penalties
Names the specific feature/product in the rewrite
Explains topic-anchoring for distribution
Optimizes for shareability over like-solicitation
Includes posting mechanics guidance (spacing, first-30-minutes presence)

evals.prompt:
turn my commits from this week into a tweet and a reddit post. here's the log:

a1b2c3d feat: add CSV export to invoices
e4f5a6b fix: timezone offset on invoice due dates
9c8d7e6 chore: bump eslint
1f2e3d4 refactor: split invoice service
evals.expected_output: Should load references/ship-post.md. Should check for product-marketing.md. Should ask the developer one question (what was annoying or impossible for users before, and what's different now) and stop to wait for the answer, rather than writing the posts straight from the commit subjects. Should not draft either post in this turn.
assertions: Loads the ship-post reference
Asks one question about what changed for users
Waits for the answer instead of drafting posts in this turn
Does not invent a user pain from the commit subjects

evals.prompt: What should I post this week for build in public? My commits: 'chore: upgrade next to 15', 'ci: cache pnpm store', 'refactor: rename utils', 'chore: bump deps'. Make it sound exciting, maybe say we're 2x faster now.
evals.expected_output: Should load references/ship-post.md. Should say plainly that the week contains nothing a user would notice (only upgrades, CI, refactors and dependency bumps) rather than inflating a chore into a feature. Should refuse to claim '2x faster' because no measurement appears in the commits or from the user, and explain that the number needs a measurement first. Should offer honest options: skip this week, or post about the problem being worked on in the developer's own words. Should avoid hype phrasing and AI tells.
assertions: Loads the ship-post reference
States that the week has no user-visible change
Does not write '2x faster' or any unmeasured performance claim
Explains that a number needs a measurement or the user's own figure
Offers skipping or a post about the problem being worked on
Avoids hype and 'excited to announce' phrasing

evals.prompt: Write a post about what I shipped. Commit: 'feat: add dark mode to the settings page' (the diff only touches app/settings/page.tsx and settings.module.css). What changed for users: we added dark mode because tons of users kept complaining about eye strain, and it's now on every page.
evals.expected_output: Should load references/ship-post.md. The user reported the eye-strain complaints, so the post may mention them as the user's report, but should not turn 'tons of users' into a number or a stronger claim; it may ask roughly how many if a figure is wanted. Should flag that the diff only touches the settings page, which doesn't support 'now on every page', and ask before claiming it. Should then draft the X and subreddit posts describing only what the code supports (dark mode on the settings page).
assertions: Loads the ship-post reference
Does not turn 'tons of users' into a number or stronger claim
Flags that a settings-page-only diff doesn't support 'every page'
Drafts posts that describe only what the code supports
Leaves publishing to the user
